SPANDANA : STARTS FORENSIC AUDIT INTO RS 7.80 CR CYBER FRAUD

• Company engaged PKF Consulting Services LLP to conduct an independent forensic audit of the cyber fraud identified on November 1, 2026
• Fraud involved unauthorised transactions from one bank account aggregating ~₹7.80 Cr transferred to multiple beneficiary accounts
• Audit to ascertain root cause and recommend remedial and preventive measures to strengthen the cybersecurity framework
• Company says business operations continue as usual and the incident has not had any material impact
Impact: Negative (cyber fraud and forensic audit create a governance and security overhang despite the stated limited business impact)

GSPLTRANS : FILES APPLICATION WITH NSE AND BSE FOR GSEG PROMOTER RECLASSIFICATION

• Follows earlier intimations dated 26 October 2026 and 3 November 2026

BERKSHIRE HATHAWAY Q3: RECORD $9.6 BN SHARE BUYBACK; CASH RESERVES AT $377 BN

• Record Buyback: Berkshire repurchased $9.6 Bn of its own shares in Q3 2026, surpassing its previous quarterly record of $9.3 Bn in Q3 2020

• Buyback Resumption: Company resumed share repurchases in March 2026 after six consecutive quarters without buybacks

• September Purchases: Spent approximately $5.4 Bn repurchasing shares at an average price of $506.64 per Class B share

• FY26 Buybacks: Total share repurchases reached approximately $14.4 Bn during the first nine months of 2026

• Equity Investments: Purchased $2.4 Bn of other companies' shares during Q3 while selling approximately $2.8 Bn, making Berkshire a modest net seller

• Buyback Comparison: Spent four times as much repurchasing its own shares as purchasing other listed equities during Q3

• Cash Reserves: Cash, cash equivalents and short-term Treasury bills stood at approximately $377.4 Bn at September-end

• Operating Earnings: Declined approximately 6% YoY to $12.71 Bn, primarily due to weaker insurance results

• Net Profit: Fell 28% YoY to $22.11 Bn, partly reflecting lower investment gains

• Leadership Strategy: CEO Greg Abel has accelerated share repurchases, reflecting a greater willingness to deploy capital

• Capital Allocation: Aggressive buybacks suggest management sees attractive value in Berkshire shares, while maintaining substantial liquidity for future investments

MUKKA : COMMENCES COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION AT OMAN FACILITY

• United Gulf Fishery Products LLC starts commercial production of fishmeal, fish oil and fish-soluble paste at Al Juba, Oman
• Group capacity rises from 291,720 MTPA to 340,170 MTPA after adding United Gulf 37,200 MTPA and Delta Marine 11,250 MTPA
• Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹508.87 Cr, up 108.06% YoY; PAT ₹17.73 Cr, up 157.51% YoY
• Secured U.S. FDA facility registration and USDA NOP inputs attestation from ECOCERT for Eco Sphere organic fertilizer
• CARE revised outlook to Stable from Negative, assigning CARE BBB- and CARE A3 to ₹480 Cr of bank facilities
• Certain shipments deferred to October 2026 due to geopolitical disruptions and supply-chain constraints
Impact: Positive (New Oman capacity plus FDA registration broaden export reach amid tight global fishmeal supply)

• Consortium of Seamec and Posh India Offshore wins LOA for subsea installation works under ONGC PRP-X pipeline replacement project

KIRAN VYAPAR : SUBSCRIBES 1.017% STAKE IN ALT MATERIAL INNOVATIONS WORTH UP TO RS 3 CR

• Company subscribed 244 Series A CCPS of Alt Material Innovations (AMIPL), equal to 1.017% of post-issue paid-up capital
• AMIPL board allotted the shares on 4 November 2026; intimation dated 3 November 2026
• Total consideration towards acquisition not exceeding ₹29.99 Cr, payable in cash
• AMIPL is a Bengaluru-based company incorporated in April 2023 into manufacturing, trading and R&D of biological materials; FY26 turnover ₹0.33 Cr, PAT ₹9.79 Cr, net worth ₹15.64 Cr
• Acquisition is strategic in nature and expected to enhance the company's business activities; no regulatory approvals required
Impact: Positive (Small-ticket strategic minority investment by the NBFC; no control or consolidation, so earnings impact is limited)

MEESHO : ACQUIRES 92.74% OF KIRANA CLUB FOR RS 186.71 CR

• Aggregate cash consideration of ₹186.71 Cr paid to identified selling shareholders
• Kirana Club has become a subsidiary and Retail Pulse Labs a step-down subsidiary of Meesho
• Kirana Club runs a digital platform for grocery retailers; Retail Pulse Labs operates a B2B marketplace connecting kirana retailers with FMCG brands, with FY26 turnover of ₹16.04 Cr
• Retail Pulse Labs FY26 net loss at ₹1.60 Cr; Kirana Club FY26 turnover SGD 45,808
• Promoters Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar are directors on the boards of both acquired entities
Impact: Positive (Adds a kirana-focused B2B commerce and retailer community platform, supporting Meesho's e-commerce ecosystem presence in Tier 2-4 and rural India)

SUPREMEINF : REDEEMS RS 25 CR NCDS, REISSUES AT 12% COUPON

• Company fully redeemed all outstanding NCDs aggregating up to ₹25 Cr issued during 2025 to a strategic global investment fund
• Subsequent new NCDs issued at a reduced coupon of 12% per annum versus the earlier 20% per annum
• No amount remains outstanding on the redeemed NCDs; obligations fully discharged
• Company expects lower borrowing and finance costs, better debt servicing and improved liquidity
• Refinancing seen optimizing capital structure and giving financial flexibility for growth initiatives
Impact: Positive (300 bps coupon cut on refinanced debt lowers interest cost and eases debt servicing burden)

SEJAL GLASS : ACQUIRES MAGNUMTUFF GLASS BUSINESS WORTH OVER RS 40 CR

• Board approved proposed Business Transfer Agreement with Magnumtuff India to acquire its Architectural Glass and Automotive Glass business undertaking on a going-concern basis via slump sale
• Aggregate lump-sum consideration of ₹40.80 Cr including purchase of the associated factory land and building
• Undertaking includes manufacturing facilities, business assets, inventory, intellectual property, technical know-how, customer and vendor relationships, contracts and employees
• Target undertaking reported operating revenue of ₹36.20 Cr in FY26
• Facility at Nainglaj Village, Chikodi Taluka, Belgaum District, Karnataka; takes manufacturing footprint to four facilities in India and targets Southern Maharashtra, Northern Karnataka and Goa markets
• Expected completion on or before November 30, 2026, subject to required transaction formalities
Impact: Positive (Adds a Karnataka glass facility and automotive glass capability, extending Sejal Glass into South India markets with a business already doing ₹36.20 Cr revenue)

CGCL : SECURES NSE IX APPROVAL FOR $30 MN BOND ISSUE

Impact: Neutral (Approval enables a USD 30 MN dollar-bond issuance; allotment is yet to be completed)

• Balance Sheet: Net debt at ₹91,423 Cr, net debt/EBITDA at 2.4x and liquidity at ₹40,076 Cr.

• H1 FY27 Performance: Revenue at ₹1,26,231 Cr; EBITDA increased 21% YoY to ₹20,035 Cr.

• Management Outlook: Focused on India volume growth, premium steel products, cost optimisation, downstream expansion and improving European operations, while monitoring raw material costs and global steel market challenges.

MSAFE : EXPANDS MANUFACTURING CAPACITY AT MATHURA

• Upcoming integrated manufacturing facility at Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, with civil construction work already underway
• Facility being developed to support capacity expansion, growth of rental business and introduction of new product categories
• Expected to commence operations by May 2027, in line with the timeline previously communicated
• Company intends to enhance manufacturing capacity for aluminium scaffolding and MS scaffolding, as outlined in its IPO plans
• Company operates a PAN-India network of 21 warehouses serving over 2,500 customers across infrastructure and construction sectors
Impact: Positive (Adds scaffolding capacity and supports rental business growth, though commissioning is only expected by May 2027)

KWALITY WALL'S Q2 FY27 ; ORGANIC SALES UP 42.2%, EBITDA AT ₹27.2 CR

RAIN INDUSTRIES : DEFERS TELANGANA CEMENT EXPANSION ON HIGH ENERGY AND FREIGHT COSTS

• Proposed cement expansion project in Telangana deferred until pricing improves enough to recover higher energy and freight costs
• Q3 cement volumes rose 11% YoY to 670 thousand tons on Priya Cement re-launch; segment adjusted EBITDA was a loss of ₹11 Cr
• Q3 revenue from operations ₹5,486 Cr, up 23% YoY; adjusted EBITDA ₹857 Cr, up 32% YoY
• Adjusted PAT ₹204 Cr, up 77% YoY, or ₹6.05 per share
• Net debt US$851 mn with net debt-to-EBITDA at 2.53x; total liquidity US$345 mn and no major term debt maturities until October 2028
• Management expects geopolitical, energy and logistics pressures to persist through Q4
Impact: Negative (Cement expansion deferral signals margin stress from elevated energy and diesel-led freight costs, with management cautious on near-term demand conditions)

• Terms to be finalised after receipt of in-principle approval from stock exchanges and other regulatory authorities
• Company was formerly known as SML Isuzu Limited; scrip codes 505192 (BSE) and SMLMAH (NSE)
Impact: Neutral (Large ₹1450 Cr rights issue funds the company but terms, pricing and dilution are yet to be decided)

• Cumulative 150 NCDs aggregating ₹150 Cr allotted out of the approved issue of up to 180 NCDs worth ₹180 Cr
• Tenure co-terminus with first tranche at 48 months from 11 March 2026, maturing 11 March 2030; redemption at par on maturity
• ISIN INE413D08016; securities are unlisted
Impact: Neutral (adds ₹40 Cr of private placement debt capital, taking cumulative NCD issuance to ₹150 Cr of the ₹180 Cr approved limit)

• Allure is developing a residential project at Sector 150, Noida, Uttar Pradesh
• Target turnover: FY26 ₹12.30 L, FY25 ₹1 L, FY24 ₹1 L

Impact: Positive (Adds a Noida residential development asset to Prestige's NCR pipeline; target turnover is negligible)

**JEFFERIES: BUY | TARGET ₹290**
- Earlier target: ₹350.

- Subsidiary stress and borrowing costs threaten margins.
- FY27–28 EPS estimates cut 1–3%.

**NIVA BUPA – BROKERAGE UPDATE**

**JEFFERIES: BUY | TARGET ₹100**
- Earlier target: ₹95.

- Improving claims ratios and new products support profitability.
- FY28–29 earnings estimates raised 5–12%.

**Power & Infrastructure**
- FY36 peak electricity demand: 459 GW.
- Current demand: 271 GW.
- Transmission investment opportunity: ₹8 lakh Cr.

**Valuations & Opportunities**
- MSCI India trades 13.4% below 10-year average.
- Banks, real estate, insurance and materials offer value.
- Lower crude benefits aviation, paints, cement, tyres and logistics.

**Key Risks**
- El Niño and weak rainfall threaten rural demand.

**JPMORGAN – INDIA EQUITY STRATEGY**

**Market Outlook**
- Bullish on Indian equities.
- Falling crude, US yields support sentiment.
- FII reversal could unlock $115 billion inflows.
- Lower crude supports rupee and corporate margins.
- Small/midcaps expected to outperform largecaps.

**Sector Allocation**
- Overweight: Financials, Industrials, Healthcare.
- Overweight: Materials, Consumer Discretionary.
- Underweight: IT.

**Growth Opportunities**
- Private capex recovery gaining momentum.
- Opportunities: Renewables, semiconductors, EVs, data centres.

- Growing awareness supports niche asset-class adoption.

**UBS: OUTPERFORM | TARGET ₹4,050**
- Q2 results exceeded expectations.
- Cash equities outperformed; normal-rate revenue accelerated.
- Lower expenses supported margins.

**BERNSTEIN: UNDERPERFORM | TARGET ₹3,180**
- CAS impacted volumes and market share.
- Earnings exceeded expectations on lower SGF contributions.
- Q3 volumes and market-share gains remain strong.

- Trading volumes expected to grow 12–15%.
- Cash equity share below management target.
- Premium valuation versus NSE remains concerning.
- Management transition expected by June 2027.

- India standalone results exceeded estimates.
- Strong revenue growth supported earnings.
- Weak EU performance impacted consolidated momentum.
- Gross margins remained under pressure.
- Monitor India demand, competition and pricing.
- Raw material costs and cost optimisation remain key.

**CITI: BUY | TARGET ₹10,770**
- Revenue/EBITDA/PAT growth: 23%/29%/32%.
- Hospital revenue increased 23%.

- Hospital EBITDA increased 20%.
- New units incurred ₹34.8 Cr expenses.
- HealthCo revenue/EBITDA grew 23%/75%.
- Digital business turned cash-positive.
- Oncology trade-margin cap and regulatory notices remain risks.

**CLSA: OUTPERFORM | TARGET ₹1,390**
- Revenue growth: 29% YoY, above expectations.
- Healthy growth across all segments.
- Margins within management guidance.
- FY27 US growth guidance: Single digit.
- India expected to outpace IPM growth.
- Margin expectation: 24%+.

**BOFA: NEUTRAL | TARGET ₹1,200**
- gAdempas and gIbrance support FY28 growth.
- Saroglitazar US launch targeted March 2027.
- Meaningful revenue expected after FY29.
- Higher commercialisation and R&D costs pressure margins.

Bernstein on Zydus Life ; Buy, TP Rs 1457

Believe revenue beat should not be overlooked

Disappointment was on costs.
EBITDA declined 150 bps more than adjusting for product mix, as investments ahead of Saroglitazar launch were higher than estimated.

Excluding them, estimate margin would have been 25.5%, vs 24% reported

Reiterate positive view on innovation story & FY28 inflection.

CITI on Aurobindo Pharma ; Sell, TP Rs 1270

Strong 2QFY27, with EBITDA/PAT beating estimates by 8%/9%, driven by robust Europe growth (+19% YoY in constant currency), slightly better-than-expected US traction & currency tailwinds.

EBITDA margin remained flat QoQ at 21%.

US sales increased 20% QoQ to US$477mn, largely driven by the Lannett consolidation

While continued strength in Europe is encouraging, driven by volume growth and market-share gains, remain cautious about its sustainability given market saturation and pricing pressure. 

Following Lannett consolidation, expect US growth to stabilize and moderate from the current pace.

KSH International ~ EBITDA/Ton Jumps 55% as Exports and Specialized Wires Drive Growth

KSH International's Q2 FY27 performance reflects improving unit economics, higher export demand and stronger balance sheet efficiency.

Key Highlights:

• Revenue Growth: +85% YoY, supported by 26% volume growth.

• EBITDA/Ton: Increased 55% from ₹65,515 to ₹1,01,454, indicating a significant improvement in profitability per ton.

• Specialized Wires: Revenue grew 87% YoY, with the segment contributing 74% of the product mix.

• Export Momentum: Export revenue surged 108% YoY, while trial HVDC export orders provide a potential new growth avenue.

• Capacity Utilisation: Reached 76% of available capacity of 57,845 MT, 96% of the planned expansion completed six months ahead of schedule.

• Deleveraging: Total debt declined 30% YoY to ₹341 Cr, while debt/equity improved from 1.38x to 0.38x.

• Working Capital: Net working capital days reduced from 70 to 52, contributing to positive operating cash flow in H1 FY27.

text:
**Arvind Fashions

A few interesting commitments:

→ Mid-double-digit revenue growth for the balance of FY27
→ 30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
→ D2C share target of ~65%, from 53% currently
→ H2 free cash flow release of ₹150–175 crore, with a large part intended for debt reduction.
Growth, channel mix and balance-sheet improvement. Worth tracking together.**

**Carborundum Universal Q2

A good example of why segment-level analysis matters.

FY27 guidance:

→ Ceramics growth raised to 25–28%
→ Ceramics margin raised to 22.5–23.5%
→ Abrasives margin lowered to 8–8.5%.
Different segments, different trajectories. Consolidated numbers may not tell the complete story.**

**Tanfac Industries Q2

Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 30% to 35–40%.

The bigger story is HFC-32:

→ 2,000–3,000 tonnes volume ramp-up in FY27
→ ~95% utilisation targeted in FY28
→ FY28 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–26%.
A significant capacity ramp-up lies ahead.**

**Dhoot Transmission Q2 

Strong growth ambitions:

→ FY27 revenue growth: 40–45%
→ FY27 capex: ~₹750 crore
→ EBITDA margin: 15–16%
→ Three additional wiring harness plants expected by mid-FY28.
Now, execution and utilisation will be key to watch.**

**GNG Electronics

Management raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~40%.
PAT margin expansion guidance also improved from 100 bps to 150 bps over FY26.
One thing to watch: inventory is expected to remain elevated through Q4 FY27.**

**PRABHUDAS LILLADHER – INDRAPRASTHA GAS (IGL)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price revised to ₹161 from ₹165.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- EBITDA loss: ₹30 Cr.
- EBITDA missed estimates significantly.
- EBITDA/scm: -₹0.30 vs ₹3.40 in Q1.
- Gas costs increased 22% QoQ, 47.9% YoY.

**Volume Performance**
- Total volumes: 10.1 mmscmd, up 8% YoY.
- CNG volumes: 7.6 mmscmd, up 8.7%.
- PNG volumes: 2.5 mmscmd, up 6%.
- Total volumes grew 4.2% QoQ.

**Margin & Supply Outlook**
- Spot LNG share increased to 15% from 3%.
- Management retains ₹6–7/scm EBITDA guidance.
- Term LNG supplies expected from Q3.
- Further supply additions expected during Q4.
- Targets approximately 10% volume growth.

**Valuation**
- Standalone business valued at 10x Sep'28E EPS.
- Investments valued at ₹21/share.
- Holding company discount: 25%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Higher spot gas costs severely impacted margins.
- Strong volume growth remains encouraging.
- Term LNG recovery is the key catalyst.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
